subject: Re: Subprocessor coverage breakdown and localization exception request
messages:
From: Simon Evans <simon.evans@finservcorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: security@clearlake.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor coverage breakdown and localization exception request

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for agreeing to chat earlier. As part of FinServeCorp's vendor intake we need: a complete list of subprocessors that touch EU production data, the country where each subprocesses' infrastructure is located, and whether we need a localization exception to keep certain telemetry or logs outside EU borders.

Two specific asks:
- A machine-readable matrix or spreadsheet with the subprocessor name, role (analytics, CDN, telemetry, KMS, observability), primary region(s), and contract/reference (DPA clause or vendor name).
- Any outstanding localization exception requests Redwood anticipates in the next 6 months (temporary fallback partners, testing enclaves, or third-party observability where locality can't be guaranteed).

We also need to surface any subprocessors that are scheduled to be added or removed in the next 60 days. Can you provide that by EOD Wednesday?

Simon Evans
Head of Vendor Risk, FinServeCorp
(simon.evans@finservcorp.com)

Attachment: vendor-onboarding-template.xlsx (FinServeCorp template)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Simon Evans <simon.evans@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor coverage breakdown and localization exception request

Simon —

Appreciate the checklist and the template. I attached a working matrix (redwood-subprocessor-matrix-2026-08-16.xlsx) that covers current subprocessors touching EU production. High-level notes up front:

- Core infra (compute + object storage): Azure EU West (Microsoft) — primary data path, no known cross-border egress for customer payloads; covered by our DPA.
- Caching/CDN: EdgeCacheCo (CDN) — EU PoPs but fall back to non-EU POPs during scale events; this is listed as a possible localization exception for limited telemetry only.
- Observability/metrics: LogSight (SaaS) — processes aggregated telemetry; we are running a pilot for an on-prem agent for EU-only retention.
- KMS/HSM: Customers can provision KMS in their VPC for Private deployments; hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys (KMS partner: KeyVaultLtd, EU keys available).

Outstanding changes (next 60 days):
- Planned: temporary addition of FastProbe (edge testing enclave) for load testing across EU/AU regions — expected Aug 28 to Sep 15. This will only see synthetic test traffic; nonetheless flagged.
- Planned: decommission of the legacy analytics worker (old-analytics-svc) in mid-September; migration to AnalyticsX.

I can't attach vendor agreements in full, but I included reference columns in the matrix with DPA clause pointers and our internal ticket IDs. If ClearLake needs evidence for a specific vendor's SOC2 or encryption attestations, loop in Kimberly and we'll assemble the package.

I can get you the finalized matrix by Wednesday EOD (your timezone) — is 2026-08-18 reasonable?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Product Security (Redwood Inference)
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-subprocessor-matrix-2026-08-16.xlsx

From: Simon Evans <simon.evans@finservcorp.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: security@clearlake.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor coverage breakdown and localization exception request

Vivek —

Thanks, that helps. Couple clarifying questions after a quick pass of the matrix:

1) For EdgeCacheCo: can you confirm whether the fallback to non-EU POPs will ever include US-based processing of any customer-generated logs (not CDN cache keys but request logs/telemetry)? We need to know if customer identifiers could cross borders.

2) For FastProbe: is the testing enclave hosted by a third-party subprocessor or a Redwood-managed ephemeral job? If third-party, please name the provider and whether they have EU residency.

3) Can you confirm the retention period for aggregated telemetry sent to LogSight and whether there is an EU-only retention flag we can elect?

If you can answer in the matrix or in a short note that would be great. Also, ClearLake may request the SOC2 snapshot for EdgeCacheCo and LogSight — I'm copying them to expedite.

Simon

On a process note: our procurement team will want a one-page localization exception form completed for any subprocessor where logs/telemetry may temporarily leave the EU. If you anticipate exceptions for EdgeCacheCo or FastProbe, please attach the filled form so legal can fast-track approvals.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Simon Evans <simon.evans@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor coverage breakdown and localization exception request

Simon —

Short answers and next steps (see attached localization-exception-form.pdf prefilled for EdgeCacheCo):

1) EdgeCacheCo fallback: request logs may be buffered at non-EU POPs during sustained scale events. Those logs include standard request metadata (timestamp, path, status, edge-POP id) and a hashed request id we use internally for troubleshooting. No PII is included by default. However, if a customer passes user identifiers in requests (e.g., user_id in payloads) those could be present in raw request logs — we flag this as a potential cross-border exposure. We recommend applying our prefix/KV caching policy (we can mask user identifiers in logs) for FinServeCorp routes to avoid export.

2) FastProbe: third-party provider is TestOrbit (EU primary, with transient workers in APAC/US for scale). TestOrbit will only run synthetic traffic and will not process real customer payloads. I've noted TestOrbit in the matrix with residency EU-primary and a planned short-term scope (Aug 28–Sep 15).

3) LogSight retention: aggregated telemetry retention is 90 days by default for hosted plans; we can enable an EU-only retention profile (30/90/365 tiers) upon request for enterprise accounts. We can set FinServeCorp to 30 days EU-only if that's required.

Attachments: localization-exception-form.pdf (prefilled: EdgeCacheCo — request logs), redwood-subprocessor-matrix-2026-08-18.xlsx (finalized columns for residency, contract clause pointers, and upcoming changes).

Action items:
- Kimberly will share SOC2 snapshots for EdgeCacheCo and LogSight by Fri 2026-08-20 (Kimberly: can you confirm?).
- Marissa will open an internal ticket to enable request-id masking on FinServeCorp routes; expected ETA Aug 24.
- Jonas will create a temporary allowlist for TestOrbit's IPs and coordinate the ephemeral workers scoping.

If FinServe wants the localization-exception signed, we can start a DocuSign flow — link in the email.

Thanks,
Vivek
